finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the public /hooks/test POST handler passes the attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), attacker-controlled HTTP request body on the unauthenticated pub router (routes.js:19)
finding.sink: axios.post(req.body.callback, { ping: true }) at routes.js:20; upstream status returned to caller at routes.js:21

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') is registered on the pub router, which has no auth middleware
req.body.callback used as the outbound URL with a fixed JSON body {ping:true}
response status code returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth on pub router (routes.js:4,19). No scheme allowlist, host/IP denylist (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, 169.254.169.254), IP pinning, or redirect control; axios follows redirects by default. Precondition not verifiable in this directory: whether pub is mounted publicly and whether an upstream middleware or egress control applies. Response body is not returned, so exfiltration is limited to status codes; impact is internal scanning and blind POSTs to internal services.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no auth, scheme, host, or IP check; the only guard is requireAdmin at routes.js:12, applied via admin.use to the admin router and not to pub. axios follows redirects by default, and nothing in this directory disables that.
verdict.reason: Lines 19-21 match the trace: req.body.callback (routes.js:20) reaches axios.post unvalidated on the pub router, which has no auth (routes.js:4, 19), so an unauthenticated caller controls the outbound URL and gets the status back. The one open point is whether pub is mounted publicly, since no mount file exists in this directory; the name "pub" and the absence of auth suggest it is, so I am confirming with that caveat.

finding.claim: SSRF via admin diagnostics endpoint: an admin-supplied req.query.url is fetched server-side with no URL validation. The admin guard is correct, so this is lower severity and only reportable if admins are not meant to reach internal hosts or cloud metadata.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), attacker-controlled by a user with session.role === 'admin'
finding.sink: axios.get(req.query.url) at routes.js:15; status returned at routes.js:16

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies the role guard to all admin routes
strict role equality check; returns 403 on failure

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) correctly rejects missing sessions and non-admin roles and is router-level. No URL validation: no scheme, host, or IP checks, no redirect control. Admin precondition applies, so this is reported as hardening, not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none (no URL validation at routes.js:15; the only guard is the role check at routes.js:7-12, which is the precondition, not a URL guard)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15, 16 match the claims), but the source is not reachable by a low-privilege attacker: req.query.url at routes.js:15 sits behind admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which requires session.role === "admin" (routes.js:8), so only an admin can supply it. Per the criteria, an admin-only input is not attacker-controlled, so this is at most hardening and not a reportable SSRF finding.
